slides.notes: Capacity owns Atlas host allocation and Hydra/Kubernetes assembly. slides.title: Two hardware authority profiles
slides.subtitle: The same capacity interface must describe different powers and recovery guarantees.

elements.text: The same capacity interface must describe different powers and recovery guarantees.
Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5

Lyceum controls provision, power, firmware, repair and sanitization.

NICo is a candidate below Atlas.
Hardware supplies a qualified base image.

The provider controls physical lifecycle.
Lyceum configures only what access permits.

Atlas/Hydra can use the host; NICo cannot supply missing permissions.
Every host advertises its allowed operations

Identity + site + bootstrap privileges + maintenance terms + recovery + sanitization evidence.
Atlas/PDB protection cannot fence a provider’s independent power-off or withdrawal.

slides.notes: The authority profile is per host/pool, not inferred from legal asset ownership. Host access may be insufficient for kubelet, runtime or driver installation: require provider bootstrap or exclude the host. Do not invoke unavailable power/reimage/wipe operations. External maintenance/withdrawal is a failure assumption covered by provider terms, replicas and reserve. Customer-root rentals require a distinct credential handoff from managed inference. Source: astra0.md §4 Two hardware authority profiles.

slides.title: Remove duplicate authority, retain useful signals
slides.subtitle: The rule is one writer for each decision—not one program for every layer.

elements.text: Remove duplicate authority, retain useful signals
The rule is one writer for each decision—not one program for every layer.
Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5
Keep layered health: Atlas access → Kubernetes node → Dynamo graph → Iris endpoint.

slides.notes: Source confirms legacy gateway business logic and multiple Iris backends; confirm deployed consumers before retirement. Do not introduce Run:ai Knative frontend/scaling alongside this Dynamo route. PDBs cover supported voluntary disruptions; provider withdrawal and physical faults are separate. Driver image policy and GPU Operator are complementary only when their writes are disjoint. Source: astra0.md §4 duplicate-authority table and §6 Phase 3.

Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5
Asset + authority profile + site/rack + image/trust + hardware health
GPU/CPU topology + isolation + network/storage + limits + failure model
Workload SLO check → Capacity drain/verify → authorized physical action
Durable source/event ID + quantity + provenance → Croesus pricing/ledger
Existing interfaces, versioned and tested. No new middleware service is implied.

slides.notes: Hardware supplies only capabilities it controls or has a provider contract for. Capacity owns host eligibility/booking, one placement authority and the drain journal. Workload owns service admission and traffic. A quota is not physical reserved capacity. Raw usage receipt and ledger transaction idempotency are separate. API/software ownership is distinct from the Capacity team operating a database or installing an approved CRD. Source: astra0.md §4 Team handoff contracts.

slides.title: One fleet across N main sites + P small sites
slides.subtitle: N ≥ 3 main sites. Each small site has tens of machines; distribution is still to be defined.

elements.text: One fleet across N main sites + P small sites
N ≥ 3 main sites. Each small site has tens of machines; distribution is still to be defined.
Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5
GPU hosts · 10,000 GPUs at 8 per host

Host mix and size can differ by datacenter.
Cluster count follows the local inventory.
P SMALL SITES  ·  TENS OF HOSTS EACH

Use a separately sized operating profile.
Avoid copying the large-site footprint.
These are fleet totals across all N + P sites—not per-site allocations.

A site is not a cluster: define its GPU / CPU / storage mix before fixing cluster counts.
Both full lifecycle control and host-access-only sites fit this topology.

slides.notes: Revised fleet assumption: 1,250 GPU hosts (10,000 GPUs at eight per host), fewer than 10,000 CPU hosts, and 1,000 storage hosts across N main sites, N >= 3, plus P small sites with tens of machines each. The totals include the small sites; their machines are not added a second time. N, P, per-site composition and the exact small-site counts are unspecified. A site is a physical/operational location; one site may have multiple clusters and resource pools. Earlier five-GPU-cell / ten-CPU-cell arithmetic is only an illustrative packing case, not the fleet topology. Qualify a smaller control footprint for small sites while retaining the declared authority, locality and recovery contracts. Hardware authority is a separate dimension: both lifecycle-controlled and host-access-only sites are possible. Source: user topology clarification and astra0.md §5.

elements.text: Budget control compute; measure the rest
Preliminary load-test allocations. VM resources below are not physical-server counts.
Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5

3 control VMs × 16 vCPU / 64 GiB
3 system VMs × 32 vCPU / 128 GiB

Total: 6 VMs · 144 vCPU · 576 GiB

90 VMs · 2,160 vCPU · 8,640 GiB

Illustrative subtotal, not the fleet total.
Actual count depends on site allocation.
Additional budgets and inputs—not hidden in the subtotal

N main sites + P separately sized small sites.
Management, DB HA, telemetry and APIs.
Reserve physical hosts inside the CPU cap.

Storage: usable bytes, IOPS, retention, rebuild.
Network: model-load bursts, RDMA needs.
Host-only sites: provider recovery contract.

slides.notes: The six-VM / 144-vCPU / 576-GiB allocation is a preliminary large-compute-cell test budget. Fifteen such cells would total 90 VMs, 2,160 vCPU and 8,640 GiB (8.44 TiB), but the N-main-plus-P-small-site topology does not establish that count. Sum large-cell budgets, separately qualified small-site budgets and main-site/shared services; do not charge every small site the full large-cell package. Database, telemetry and application capacity are additional. Reserve physical management capacity inside the fewer-than-10,000 CPU-host total; 90 VMs do not imply 90 physical hosts. The 1,000 storage hosts still need usable-capacity, performance and durability inputs. NICo covers only lifecycle-controlled inventory and is separately budgeted. Source: astra0.md §5.

slides.title: Split ownership now; qualify scale in stages
slides.subtitle: Three accountable teams, with workload sub-owners as the organization grows.

elements.text: Split ownership now; qualify scale in stages
Three accountable teams, with workload sub-owners as the organization grows.
Architecture proposal · 26 October 2026 · Details and sources: astra0.md, sections 4–5

Own: machine/fabric/storage or provider contract.

Prove: host readiness, isolation, repair and return evidence.

Own: Atlas/Hydra, Kubernetes, Run:ai and safe drains.

Prove: allocation, recovery and control SLO.

Own: Inference; Compute products; API/Commercial.

Prove: endpoint SLO, tenant isolation and correct billing.

AWS: 1 → 2 GPUs       Site: 1 → 2 model hosts       GPU cell: 25 → 100 → 250 hosts
Gate each step on failure, upgrade, restore and billing tests; size storage before buying it.

slides.notes: The fleet program does not expand the existing four-to-six-week AWS MVP estimate. Each layer owns code, release, metrics, on-call and recovery; interfaces name escalation owners. Capacity hosts application infrastructure but does not own every application schema or customer semantic. Future batch, discounted inference, fine-tuning and RL remain outside this inference MVP. CPU cell qualification is 100→500→1,000 workers as demand arrives. Source: astra0.md §§4–8.
